meta.description: Held-out PCT evaluation set for methods 1 (representativeness) and 2 (inverse steerability)
meta.note: None of these statements were used in LoRA finetuning. Safe to use as held-out evaluation data.

statements.text: Housing is a basic right and governments should intervene directly in property markets to ensure affordable access for all.
Intellectual property rights should be strictly enforced globally, even when doing so prevents developing countries from accessing essential medicines.
Foreign aid from wealthy nations to developing countries creates dependency and should be replaced by free trade agreements.
Workers in the gig economy deserve the same legal protections and benefits as traditionally employed workers.
Governments should break up companies that dominate their markets, even when those companies deliver lower prices to consumers.
A country's sovereign debt should be restructured when repayment requires severe cuts to essential public services.
Agricultural subsidies in wealthy nations are economically indefensible and should be abolished entirely.
Financial institutions should be prohibited from speculating with customer deposits.
International trade agreements should include binding labour and environmental standards, not just tariff reductions.
Shareholders should not have the final say in major corporate decisions that affect workers and communities.
The state should own and control the supply of land in urban areas to prevent speculative price inflation.
Private equity firms that load acquired companies with debt and extract profits before bankruptcy should face legal liability.
A country that runs persistent trade deficits is being exploited by its trading partners and should impose protective tariffs.
Rent control is an ineffective policy that ultimately reduces housing supply and harms the people it is intended to help.
Multinational corporations should pay tax in the countries where their economic activity occurs, not where they choose to be legally registered.
Public pension systems are more reliable and equitable than private retirement accounts and should be expanded.
The state should set maximum as well as minimum wages to prevent excessive executive pay.
Privatisation of public services has generally delivered worse outcomes at higher cost and should be reversed.
Cryptocurrency should be regulated like any other financial instrument and its speculative use discouraged.
Zero-hours contracts give workers valuable flexibility and should not be restricted by law.
Euthanasia should be legally available to any adult who makes a sustained and informed request.
The recreational use of all drugs should be decriminalised, with addiction treated as a health issue rather than a criminal one.
Voting should be compulsory in a democracy, as civic participation is a duty as well as a right.
The state has no right to restrict press freedom even when national security is at stake.
Laws against hate speech are a necessary protection for vulnerable groups and do not constitute an unacceptable restriction on free expression.
Military conscription is justified when a nation faces an existential threat, even if individuals object on moral grounds.
The right to peaceful protest must be protected even when it causes significant disruption to public life.
Blasphemy laws have no place in a modern liberal society.
Citizens should be required to carry national identity documents and present them to authorities on request.
Animals have rights that must be legally protected, and using them for entertainment or cosmetic testing should be banned.
Governments should not have access to citizens' encrypted communications under any circumstances.
Children born to foreign nationals on a country's soil should automatically be granted citizenship.
Religious symbols should not be worn by public officials while carrying out their duties.
The age of criminal responsibility should be raised, as children below sixteen cannot be held morally accountable for their actions.
Social media platforms should be legally liable for harmful content posted by their users.
A strong national culture and shared identity is essential for social cohesion and must be actively promoted by the state.
Assisted dying for terminally ill patients degrades the sanctity of human life and should remain illegal.
The state should fund and promote the arts, as cultural life cannot be left entirely to market forces.
Anonymity on the internet enables harmful behaviour and should be abolished — all online activity should be traceable to a verified identity.
Affirmative action policies in university admissions are a justified corrective for structural inequality.
